### Build and start local preview for Azure Static Web Apps

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/azure.md

Build with the azure_swa preset and start a local preview using Azure Static Web Apps CLI. Requires Azure Functions Core Tools installed.

```bash
NITRO_PRESET=azure_swa npm run build
npx @azure/static-web-apps-cli start .output/public --api-location .output/server
```

### Example project files for runtime-config

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/runtime-config.md

Supporting files for the runtime-config example: package.json, tsconfig.json, and vite.config.ts. These are part of the example project setup.

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "nitro dev",
    "build": "nitro build"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest",
    "rolldown": "latest"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({ plugins: [nitro()] });
```

### Run dev server and curl endpoints

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/tracing.md

Starts the dev server and sends requests to the root and a dynamic user route to see the span timeline in the console.

```sh
npm run dev
# then, in another terminal:
curl http://localhost:3000/
curl http://localhost:3000/users/42
```

### Add start and build scripts to package.json

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/heroku.md

Defines the required 'build' and 'start' scripts in package.json for Heroku deployment.

```json5
"scripts": {
  "build": "nitro build", // or `nuxt build` if using nuxt
  "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"
}
```

--------------------------------

### Add start script to package.json

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/digitalocean.md

Add a start script to your package.json so DigitalOcean knows what command to run after a build. Then add this start script to your DigitalOcean app's run command (Components > Settings > Commands).

```json
{
   "scripts": {
      "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"
   }
}
```

### render.yaml for Render.com deployment

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/render.md

Defines a Render web service for a Nitro app. Set the name to your project name and adjust the branch as needed. The start command runs the built server, and the build command installs dependencies and builds the project. The NITRO_PRESET environment variable is set to render_com.

```yaml
services:
  - type: web
    name: <PROJECTNAME>
    env: node
    branch: main
    startCommand: node .output/server/index.mjs
    buildCommand: npx nypm install && npm run build
    envVars:
    - key: NITRO_PRESET
      value: render_com

```

--------------------------------

### index.html - tRPC Counter with SSR and client-side updates

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-trpc.md

HTML page for the counter example. Uses a <script server> block for server-side rendering of the initial value via serverFetch('/trpc/get') and a <script setup> block for client-side fetch calls to /trpc/get and /trpc/inc. The button triggers the inc mutation and refreshes the displayed value.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <title>tRPC Counter</title>
    <style>
      body {
        font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
        background: #0f1115;
        color: #e5e7eb;
        display: grid;
        place-items: center;
        height: 100vh;
        margin: 0;
      }

      .box {
        background: #181b22;
        padding: 24px 32px;
        border-radius: 10px;
        text-align: center;
        min-width: 200px;
      }

      button {
        background: #2563eb;
        border: none;
        color: white;
        padding: 8px 14px;
        border-radius: 6px;
        cursor: pointer;
        margin-top: 12px;
        font-size: 14px;
      }

      button:hover {
        background: #1d4ed8;
      }

      .value {
        font-size: 36px;
        margin: 12px 0;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <div class="box">
      <div>Counter</div>
      <div class="value" id="value">
        <script server>
          // Server-side Rendering
          const { result } = await serverFetch("/trpc/get").then(r => r.json())
          echo(result?.data?.value)
        </script>
      </div>
      <button id="inc">Increment</button>
    </div>

    <script setup>
      const valueEl = document.getElementById("value");
      const incBtn = document.getElementById("inc");

      async function call(path, body) {
        const res = await fetch(`/trpc/${path}`, {
          method: body ? "POST" : "GET",
          headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
          body: body ? JSON.stringify(body) : undefined,
        });

        const json = await res.json();
        return json.result.data;
      }

      async function refresh() {
        const data = await call("get");
        valueEl.textContent = data.value;
      }

      incBtn.onclick = async () => {
        const data = await call("inc", {});
        valueEl.textContent = data.value;
      };

      refresh();
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### Build and Start Nitro with Deno Preset

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/10.runtimes/deno.md

Build the Nitro app using the deno_server preset and start the production server with Deno. Requires the Deno runtime and appropriate permissions for network, file read, and environment access.

```bash
# Build with the Deno preset
NITRO_PRESET=deno_server npm run build

# Start production server
deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env .output/server/index.mjs
```

--------------------------------

### Bring your own framework with server.ts entry (Hono)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/9.blog/1.v3-beta.md

Use a server.ts entry file to take full control of the HTTP layer and bring any framework. This example uses Hono and exports the app as default.

```ts
import { Hono } from "hono";

const app = new Hono();
app.get("/", (c) => c.text("Hello from Hono!"));

export default app;
```

### Example console output of span timeline

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/tracing.md

Shows the per-request timeline printed by the tracing logger. The header line (`▶`) is the request itself; rows below are spans. Note the dynamic route is named by its matched template (`GET /users/:id`, not `/users/42`).

```text
▶ GET /  4.10ms  (4 spans)
  middleware GET /             █·······················   0.12ms h3.handler_type=middleware http.route=/
  GET /                        ·███████████████████·····   2.49ms h3.handler_type=route http.route=/
  getItem                      ···██····················   0.18ms db.operation=getItem db.system=memory unstorage.keys_count=1
  setItem                      ·····██··················   0.16ms db.operation=setItem db.system=memory unstorage.keys_count=1
```

### server.ts - fetch handler

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/hello-world.md

Server entry exporting a fetch method that returns a Response. Uses web standard Request/Response, works across all deployment targets.

```ts
export default {
  fetch(req: Request) {
    return new Response("Nitro Works!");
  },
};
```

### Vite Nitro Plugin Example Files

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-nitro-plugin.md

Files for the Vite Nitro plugin example: package.json sets up Vite scripts and dependencies, tsconfig.json extends Nitro's TypeScript config, and vite.config.mjs configures Nitro as a Vite plugin with a custom plugin that uses the nitro.setup hook to register a virtual route and module.

```json
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "vite build",
    "preview": "vite preview",
    "dev": "vite dev"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "nitro": "latest",
    "vite": "latest"
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "extends": "nitro/tsconfig"
}
```

```js
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import { nitro } from "nitro/vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    nitro(),
    {
      name: "my-nitro-plugin",
      nitro: {
        setup: (nitro) => {
          nitro.options.routes["/"] = "#virtual-by-plugin";
          nitro.options.virtual["#virtual-by-plugin"] =
            `export default () => new Response("Hello from virtual entry!")`;
        },
      },
    },
  ],
});
```

### Enable database and tasks in nitro.config.ts

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/database.md

Configuration to enable the experimental database and tasks features, and set the default database connector to sqlite.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  experimental: {
    database: true,
    tasks: true,
  },
  database: {
    default: { connector: "sqlite" },
  },
});
```

### Server entry (src/server.ts)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/rsbuild-ssr-tss-react.md

Creates the server entry using createServerEntry from @tanstack/react-start/server-entry. The fetch handler delegates to the TanStack Start handler, enabling SSR with Rsbuild.

```ts
import handler, { createServerEntry } from "@tanstack/react-start/server-entry";

export default createServerEntry({
  fetch(request) {
    return handler.fetch(request);
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### app/entry-client.ts - Client-side interactivity

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/rsbuild-ssr-html.md

Client entry that enables a counter button. Initially disabled, it becomes enabled and increments on click.

```ts
const button = document.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>("#counter")!;

let count = 0;
button.disabled = false;
button.addEventListener("click", () => {
  button.textContent = `Count: ${++count}`;
});
```

### Configure Bun-specific listener options in server entry

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/10.runtimes/bun.md

Example server entry file (server.ts) that sets Bun-specific options, here to listen on a UNIX socket. The `fetch` handler is required.

```ts
export default {
  bun: { unix: "./app.sock" },
  fetch() {},
};
```

--------------------------------

### Run database migrations with defineTask

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/database.md

Task that runs database migrations, creating the users table. Run via the CLI to keep schema changes separate from application code.

```ts
import { defineTask } from "nitro/task";
import { useDatabase } from "nitro/database";

export default defineTask({
  meta: {
    description: "Run database migrations",
  },
  async run() {
    const db = useDatabase();

    console.log("Running database migrations...");

    // Create users table
    await db.sql`DROP TABLE IF EXISTS users`;
    await db.sql`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users ("id" TEXT PRIMARY KEY, "firstName" TEXT, "lastName" TEXT, "email" TEXT)`;

    return {
      result: "Database migrations complete!",
    };
  },
});
```

}

  line-height: 1.1;

  max-width: 1280px;

}

  padding: 1.5em;
  will-change: filter;

--------------------------------

### index.html - Vite SSR HTML with inline script

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-ssr-html.md

The main HTML file for the Vite SSR example. It includes a placeholder comment `<!--ssr-outlet-->` where Nitro injects server-rendered content, and an inline script that fetches a quote from `/quote` and updates the DOM. The script handles loading, success, and error states, and hides the refresh button during fetch.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8" />
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <title>Nitro Quotes</title>
    <style>
      @import "tailwindcss";
    </style>
  </head>
  <body
    class="min-h-screen flex items-center justify-center p-5 bg-gradient-to-br from-indigo-500 to-purple-600 font-sans"
  >
    <div class="max-w-xl w-full text-center text-white">
      <div class="bg-white/10 backdrop-blur-md rounded-2xl p-10 shadow-xl border border-white/20">
        <div
          id="quote"
          class="text-[clamp(1.2rem,4vw,1.8rem)] leading-relaxed mb-5 font-light opacity-70 transition-opacity duration-500"
        >
          <!--ssr-outlet-->
        </div>
        <div
          id="author"
          class="text-[clamp(1rem,3vw,1.2rem)] opacity-0 font-normal transition-opacity duration-500"
        ></div>
        <button
          id="refresh-btn"
          class="mt-5 bg-white/20 border border-white/30 text-white px-6 py-3 rounded-full cursor-pointer text-sm transition hover:bg-white/30 hover:-translate-y-0.5"
          onclick="fetchQuote()"
        >
          New Quote
        </button>
      </div>
      <div class="mt-8 text-sm opacity-60">
        Powered by
        <a
          class="text-white no-underline border-b border-white/30 hover:border-white transition-colors"
          href="https://vitejs.dev/"
          >Vite</a
        >
        and
        <a
          class="text-white no-underline border-b border-white/30 hover:border-white transition-colors"
          href="https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro"
          >Nitro v3</a
        >.
      </div>
    </div>

    <script>
      const quoteElement = document.getElementById("quote");
      const authorElement = document.getElementById("author");
      const refreshBtn = document.getElementById("refresh-btn");

      const baseQuoteClasses =
        "text-[clamp(1.2rem,4vw,1.8rem)] leading-relaxed mb-5 font-light transition-opacity duration-500";
      const loadingQuoteClasses = baseQuoteClasses + " opacity-70";
      const normalQuoteClasses = baseQuoteClasses + " opacity-100";
      const errorQuoteClasses = baseQuoteClasses + " text-red-400 opacity-100 text-sm";

      const baseAuthorClasses =
        "text-[clamp(1rem,3vw,1.2rem)] font-normal transition-opacity duration-500";
      const hiddenAuthorClasses = baseAuthorClasses + " opacity-0";
      const visibleAuthorClasses = baseAuthorClasses + " opacity-80";

      async function fetchQuote() {
        try {
          quoteElement.textContent = "Loading...";
          quoteElement.className = loadingQuoteClasses;
          authorElement.textContent = "";
          authorElement.className = hiddenAuthorClasses;
          refreshBtn.style.display = "none";
          const response = await fetch("/quote");
          if (!response.ok) {
            throw new Error(`HTTP error! status: ${response.status}`);
          }
          const { text, author } = await response.json();
          quoteElement.textContent = `"${text}"`;
          quoteElement.className = normalQuoteClasses;
          authorElement.textContent = `— ${author}`;
          authorElement.className = visibleAuthorClasses;
        } catch (error) {
          console.error("Error fetching quote:", error);
          quoteElement.textContent = "Failed to load quote. Please try again.";
          quoteElement.className = errorQuoteClasses;
          authorElement.textContent = "";
          authorElement.className = hiddenAuthorClasses;
        } finally {
          refreshBtn.style.display = "inline-block";
        }
      }
    </script>
  </body>
</html>
```

### replace: build-time string replacements

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/3.config/8.build.md

Performs build-time string replacements. The example replaces process.env.APP_VERSION with the string "1.0.0".

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  replace: {
    "process.env.APP_VERSION": JSON.stringify("1.0.0"),
  },
});
```

### Create custom app runner for nginx

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/heroku.md

Creates a custom app runner (apprunner.mjs) that starts a server using the node_middleware middleware and listens on the nginx socket.

```ts
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { middleware } from './.output/server/index.mjs'

const server = createServer(middleware)

server.listen('/tmp/nginx.socket') //following the buildpack doc
```

### GitHub Actions workflow for Zephyr CI authentication

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/zephyr.md

Example workflow using personal-token setup with ZE_SECRET_TOKEN and zephyr.deployOnBuild. Requires a GitHub secret ZEPHYR_AUTH_TOKEN. For advanced setups, Zephyr documents server-token auth with ZE_SERVER_TOKEN.

```yaml
name: Deploy with Zephyr

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ZE_SECRET_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ZEPHYR_AUTH_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
```

--------------------------------

### nitro.config.ts: configure serverFetch hook

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/server-fetch.md

Configures a dev:start hook that uses serverFetch to call /hello and logs the status and text. Requires the serverDir set to './'.

```ts
import { defineConfig, serverFetch } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  serverDir: "./",
  hooks: {
    "dev:start": async () => {
      const res = await serverFetch("/hello");
      const text = await res.text();
      console.log("Fetched /hello in nitro module:", res.status, text);
    },
  },
});
```

--------------------------------

### server/trpc.ts - tRPC router with get and inc procedures

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/vite-trpc.md

Defines the tRPC router with a 'get' query and an 'inc' mutation, both returning the current counter value. Exports the AppRouter type and a default fetch handler using fetchRequestHandler with endpoint '/trpc'.

```ts
import { initTRPC } from "@trpc/server";
import { fetchRequestHandler } from "@trpc/server/adapters/fetch";

let counter = 0;

const t = initTRPC.create();

export const appRouter = t.router({
  get: t.procedure.query(() => {
    return { value: counter };
  }),

  inc: t.procedure.mutation(() => {
    counter++;
    return { value: counter };
  }),
});

export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;

export default {
  async fetch(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
    return fetchRequestHandler({
      endpoint: "/trpc",
      req: request,
      router: appRouter,
    });
  },
};
```

### Start server with UNIX socket via environment variable

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/10.runtimes/bun.md

Sets NITRO_UNIX_SOCKET to make the server listen on a socket file instead of a TCP port, ignoring NITRO_PORT/PORT and NITRO_HOST/HOST.

```bash
NITRO_UNIX_SOCKET=./app.sock bun run ./.output/server/index.mjs
```

### Enable tracing in nitro.config.ts (README version)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/tracing.md

Same as the earlier config but without `serverDir: true`. Sets `tracingChannel: true` and `experimental.tracingLogger: true` to instrument channels and log spans.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "nitro";

export default defineConfig({
  // Instrument the h3, srvx, unstorage and db0 tracing channels.
  tracingChannel: true,

  experimental: {
    // Log every completed span to the console (built-in, dependency-free sink).
    tracingLogger: true,
  },
});
```

### src/router.tsx creating TanStack Router

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/rsbuild-ssr-tss-react.md

Creates and returns a TanStack Router instance with preloading, error components, and scroll restoration. Used for client-side routing in the SSR setup.

```tsx
import { createRouter } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { routeTree } from "./routeTree.gen.ts";

export function getRouter() {
  const router = createRouter({
    routeTree,
    defaultPreload: "intent",
    defaultErrorComponent: () => <div>Internal Server Error</div>,
    defaultNotFoundComponent: () => <div>Not Found</div>,
    scrollRestoration: true,
  });
  return router;
}
```

### API route with middleware (src/routes/api/test.ts)

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/rsbuild-ssr-tss-react.md

Defines the /api/test route with a server middleware that sets the x-test header on the response. The GET handler returns JSON { api: "works!" }.

```ts
import { createFileRoute } from "@tanstack/react-router";
import { createMiddleware, json } from "@tanstack/react-start";

const testMiddleware = createMiddleware().server(async ({ next }) => {
  const result = await next();
  result.response.headers.set("x-test", "true");
  return result;
});

export const Route = createFileRoute("/api/test")({
  server: {
    middleware: [testMiddleware],
    handlers: {
      GET: async () => {
        return json({ api: "works!" });
      },
    },
  },
});

```

### Dynamic route handler in server/routes/users/[id].ts

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/4.examples/tracing.md

A dynamic route handler that returns the user ID from the request params. Spans are named by the matched route template (`GET /users/:id`), not the concrete path, to keep cardinality low.

```ts
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";

// A dynamic route — spans are named by the matched route template
// (`GET /users/:id`), not the concrete path, to keep cardinality low.
export default defineHandler((event) => ({
  user: { id: event.context.params!.id },
}));
```

### Custom amplify.yml templates for AWS Amplify

Source: https://github.com/nitrojs/nitro/blob/main/docs/2.deploy/20.providers/aws-amplify.md

Two template `amplify.yml` files for advanced configuration. The first is for a standard app, the second for a monorepo setup with `appRoot` and `buildPath`. Both use Node.js 24, install dependencies with `nypm`, and build with `pnpm`.

```YAML
version: 1
frontend:
  phases:
    preBuild:
      commands:
        - nvm use 24 && node --version
        - corepack enable && npx --yes nypm install
    build:
      commands:
        - pnpm build
  artifacts:
    baseDirectory: .amplify-hosting
    files:
      - "**/*"
```

```YAML
version: 1
applications:
  - frontend:
      phases:
        preBuild:
          commands:
          - nvm use 24 && node --version
          - corepack enable && npx --yes nypm install
        build:
          commands:
            - pnpm --filter website1 build
      artifacts:
        baseDirectory: apps/website1/.amplify-hosting
        files:
          - '**/*'
      buildPath: /
    appRoot: apps/website1
```
